title: Gamescom Is the Biggest Gaming Show Ever — and It's Not Stressed About It!
summary:
Have you ever been to a giant gaming festival? Imagine a place where thousands of people gather to see new video games, meet their favorite streamers, and even watch people beat games super fast. That place is Gamescom, and it's now the biggest gaming event in the whole world!

Gamescom started back in 2002 in Germany. For a long time, it was just Europe's big gaming show. But then E3, the huge American gaming event, closed down after the pandemic. So now, all eyes are on Gamescom. People from everywhere watch its big opening show, called Opening Night Live, where game makers reveal new trailers and surprises.

You might think the people who run Gamescom would feel super stressed. But guess what? They say they're not stressed at all! Tim Endres, one of the bosses, said they're actually happy and excited that more people are watching. Another boss, Stefan Heikhaus, said they feel a responsibility to make it great, but it's more like excitement than pressure.

This year, Gamescom is adding something really cool: Games Done Quick, or GDQ for short. GDQ is a famous event where people speedrun games — that means playing them as fast as possible. This is the first time GDQ is happening outside of North America! It'll be three days of nonstop speedrunning, from August 28 to 30, and it's all for charity.

Gamescom is also thinking about the future. They want to keep growing, but they're not planning to start a big event in North America. Instead, they're focusing on their home in Cologne, Germany, and their events in Asia and Latin America.

So if you love games, keep an eye on Gamescom. It's the place where gaming's biggest moments happen — and it's only getting bigger!
why_it_matters: If you love video games, Gamescom is where new games and fun gaming trends are first shown, so it can help you discover what you might play next.

background_read: Gamescom (a giant video-game festival in Germany) started in 2002.
E3 (a famous American gaming show) used to be one of the biggest gaming events in the world, but it stopped after the pandemic.
Games Done Quick (GDQ) is a speedrunning marathon where players finish games as fast as they can to raise money for charity.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tim Endres and Stefan Heikhaus run Gamescom, and gamers, streamers, and speedrunners take part.
WHAT: Gamescom is the biggest gaming event in the world, with new trailers, live shows, and a new GDQ speedrunning event for charity.
WHERE: Gamescom happens in Cologne, Germany, and the organizers also hold events in Asia and Latin America.
WHY: With E3 gone, Gamescom is now the center of gaming news, and its bosses feel excited rather than stressed about being bigger.
